name: @forguncy-react-workspace/core
//exports: `./browser` is the browser-safe projection of this package's surface: the same
decisions, on a graph with no `node:` builtin in it (see `src/browser.ts`). It
exists because a barrel re-export is not a declaration — importing one name from
`.` evaluated `cell-registry` and `config-loader` too, and their module-scope
`node:fs`/`node:path` destructuring broke both a browser dev graph and a compiled
Cell artifact. `cell-registry` and `config-loader` are genuinely node-side and are
deliberately absent from it; `browser.test.ts` asserts that, and asserts the two
surfaces agree in both directions rather than letting this entry grow its own API.
`./cell-props` is the leaf the production Cell runtime binds to (#124): the two pure key
tuples a compiled Cell needs (`CELL_PROPS_BASE_KEYS`, `CELL_FORGUNCY_PROP_KEYS`), with no
imports at all. It exists because those tuples used to be derived inside
`runtime-contract.ts`, which carries the evidence record that explains them — so reading
two keys meant loading every execution fact and open question into a flat Cell artifact.
The tuples are still defined once; `runtime-contract.ts` imports them and re-exports the
same bindings, so this subpath is a smaller *graph*, not a second definition.
`cell-props.test.ts` asserts it reaches nothing and that the values are the record's own.
`./internal` is the full projection of this package's modules (#159): the surface the root
entry used to export, kept for this package's own tests. No other package may import it, and
`package-boundaries.test.ts` asserts that rule for every package.
